newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index call buying up slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index call buying up slightly.

text.p: Index call option buyers became a little more aggressive as the market continued to rally on Wednesday, but put buying remained persistent, traders said.

Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX (S&P 100 index) at the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), said index options trading was moderate, with at-the-money call buying the main action.
"You are seeing both sides of the market, but predominantly calls," he said, adding that put buyers were likely hedging portfolios or anticipating a market consolidation.
In the last couple of weeks, put buying has consistently outpaced call buying, providing a strong indicator for contrarian investors that the market would remain strong.
According to Jerry Hegarty at Thomson Financial Services, in the last two trading days, OEX put volume has topped call volume by a total of 101,000 contracts.
"This pace is bullish in the long run and will most likely lead to higher prices," he said in a report.
An SPX (S&P 500 index) options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said a big trading house had been actively buying December 685 calls in morning trading.
"I'm not exactly sure if they were getting out of something from a while ago or if it was just some sort of money play," he said, adding the firm paid from 59.10 to 62.55 for the options.
He said that despite continued steady put buying, investors did not appear to be growing more nervous as the market continued to probe into record territory.
"I would imagine people are watching to see if the roof stays or not because it's been looking strong for no apparent reason," he said.
"Since the (November 5 presidential) election we've had one down day on the Dow (industrial average), so we have to be approaching some sort of nervous area," he added. "But the sentiment seems good.
"Who wants to stand in front of a moving train?"
At 1210 CST (1810 GMT), the blue chip Dow industrial average .DJI was up 15 points at nearly 6,413, off its intraday high of 6,438.59, a record.
Traders said index options investors were playing the market's choppiness, as both the SPX and OEX flirted with higher strike prices.
The SPX was up a fraction at about 742.50 after climbing early to 744.28, just shy of the 745 strike price.
The OEX was ahead about half a point at around 717 after rising to 719.45, just below the 720 strike price.
The heaviest volume in OEX options was in the December 715 puts, which traded 6,170 contracts. The December 715 call was the most active call, with about 3,070 contracts traded.
Among SPX options, the most active options were the December 735 and 745 puts, each of which traded more than 3,800 contracts.
